dedupe_keys.name: gnss satellite visibility analysis in urban areas with lidar superimposed columns lu and han isprs 2020

description: This ISPRS Congress paper proposes a superimposed column method to analyse the surroundings of a GNSS receiver in urban areas, where dense buildings block satellite signals and weaken positioning. It combines airborne LiDAR point clouds with a 2D building boundary map to build reliable 3D spatial information, reconstructs buildings as columns, and computes obstruction and satellite visibility to find the best observation time of day. Compared with the original LiDAR data and a raster approach, the column data are about 3 percent of the data amount and take 0.003 percent of the calculation time, with about 3.3 degrees RMSD against the original LiDAR result. Producer: Ya-Hsuan Lu and Jen-Yu Han, National Taiwan University; published in ISPRS Archives volume XLIII-B4-2020. Coverage: a test urban area in Taiwan. Access: free PDF on the ISPRS Archives site. Licence and cost: free; the footer states CC BY 4.0. Caveats: no code is released, and results are for the test datasets in the paper. Simulation uses: it gives an efficient obstruction and visibility model for GNSS availability and planning in dense urban environments. Related record: Trimble GNSS Planning (platform-trimble-gnss-planning), a commercial planning tool.
